evidence: Wikipedia's Funkadelic article names Sly Stone, with Jimi Hendrix, the MC5 and Vanilla Fudge, among the band's major inspirations. Funkadelic released 'The Naz' in 2013, a collaboration with Sly Stone. The influence is widely repeated in histories of funk rather than pinned to one statement, so it is tiered consensus.

earlier.title: Thank You (Falettinme Be Mice Elf Agin)

trackPair.whatToListenFor: On 'Thank You', Larry Graham's bass is thumped and plucked so hard it becomes the lead instrument, and the vocal lines pass between several singers instead of staying with one. 'Up for the Down Stroke' does the same with a bigger crowd: the bass is up front, and the vocals are chants and call-and-response from the whole group. The idea of the band as a gang of voices, with the bass in charge, is what P-Funk took from Sly.

explanation: Sly and the Family Stone mixed soul, rock and psychedelic sounds, gave the bass a starring role, and shared the singing around a whole band of men and women, Black and white. George Clinton's Parliament and Funkadelic are usually described as taking that idea and making it bigger and wilder, a collective of dozens. Much later, in 2013, Funkadelic even made a song with Sly Stone. It is held at consensus: the influence is standard in funk histories and in Funkadelic's own listed inspirations, but it rests on the pattern of the records rather than on one documented statement.
